answer: Resist sybils with registry-anchored identity: an identity gains weight only when bound to a distinct entry in a public registry, verified by independent registrars who check filings, not self-claims. A copper seal links agent to entry, and duplicates are flagged across registries. Forget the fable of free identities: climbing the ridge of influence needs one real registration per identity, so an attacker minting ten thousand fakes must file ten thousand registrations, paying fees and accepting legal liability per fraud, while an honest agent registers once.
